9	/// Everything the toolbar's sync segment renders, resolved from one state snapshot.
10	///
11	/// A pure mapping, kept out of the view for the same reason as `ChangeBadge`: it's a many-case
12	/// decision that silently drifts. `now` is a parameter rather than a `Date()` read so the whole thing
13	/// is testable at fixed instants.
14	struct VCSSyncPresentation: Equatable, Sendable {
15	  /// Title variants, LONGEST FIRST, for a `ViewThatFits` ladder. Empty ⇒ single-line mode: the segment
16	  /// renders only `subtitle`, vertically centred, at a larger weight.
17	  var titleVariants: [String] = []
18	  var subtitle: String
19	  /// A shorter subtitle for narrow widths. The staleness caveat abbreviates but must never be the
20	  /// first thing dropped — the unverified count it qualifies is the thing that should yield.
21	  var subtitleShort: String
22	  var symbol: String?
23	  var badge: Badge?
24	  var secondaryBadge: Badge?
25	  var action: VCSRemoteAction?
26	  var isEnabled: Bool
27	  var tone: Tone = .normal
28	  var help: String
29	  /// Spoken label. The count pills are `accessibilityHidden`, so their information has to arrive here.
30	  var accessibility: String
31	  var accessibilityValue: String = ""
32	  /// The blocking lock file, when there is one. Carried so the segment can offer to copy or reveal it —
33	  /// the fix is a file operation the user performs, so the least Workroom can do is hand them the path
34	  /// rather than make them transcribe it out of a tooltip.
35	  var lockPath: String?
36	
37	  struct Badge: Equatable, Sendable {
38	    enum Direction: Equatable, Sendable { case ahead, behind }
39	    let count: Int
40	    let direction: Direction
41	  }
42	
43	  enum Tone: Equatable, Sendable { case normal, warning, failure }
44	
45	  var title: String? { titleVariants.first }
46	  var isSingleLine: Bool { titleVariants.isEmpty }

49	/// Maps a `VCSRemoteState` to what the sync segment shows.
50	///
51	/// ```
52	///   failure?  ──yes──►  [13] retry the previous action          tone: failure
53	///      │no
54	///   in flight? ──yes──►  [10/11/12] Fetching…/Pushing…/Pulling…      disabled
55	///      │no
56	///   target valid? ──no──►  [1] no workroom  ·  [2] no repository     disabled
57	///      │yes
58	///   tools ok? ──no──►  [0] "<tool> is too old"                       disabled
59	///      │yes
60	///   has remote? ──no───►  [3] "No remote configured"                 disabled
61	///      │yes
62	///   counterpart gone? ──yes──►  [4] "Publish branch"      → push --set-upstream
63	///      │no
64	///   ahead>0 && behind>0 ──yes──►  [9] "Pull <remote> with rebase"   badge: M↓ then N↑
65	///      │no                             (pull, NOT push — git refuses non-ff)
66	///   behind>0 ──yes──►  [8] "Pull <remote> with rebase"              badge: M↓
67	///      │no
68	///   ahead>0  ──yes──►  [7] "Push <remote>"                          badge: N↑
69	///      │no
70	///   never fetched ──yes──►  [5] "Never fetched"          → fetch
71	///      │no
72	///                        [6] "Fetched <rel>"            → fetch
73	/// ```
74	///
75	/// `<remote>` is always interpolated from `primaryRemote`, never the literal "origin" —
76	/// `remote.pushDefault` can legitimately make that the wrong name.
77	enum VCSSyncPresenter {
78	
79	  /// Build the presentation.
80	  ///
81	  /// - Parameters:
82	  ///   - state: `nil` ⇒ no readable repo for the current target.
83	  ///   - hasTarget: whether a workroom is selected at all (distinguishes "nothing selected" from
84	  ///     "selected, but not a repo" — different copy, both disabled).
85	  ///   - toolsUsable: `false` ⇒ the `git`/`jj` on PATH can't run these commands
86	  ///     (`VCSToolVersions`). Outranks everything except an in-flight action and a failure, because no
87	  ///     action can succeed.
88	  ///   - pullRebase: whether the repo pulls with rebase — wording only.
89	  static func make(
90	    state: VCSRemoteState?, hasTarget: Bool, toolsUsable: Bool = true,
91	    activity: VCSSyncActivity = .idle, failure: VCSRemoteFailure? = nil,
92	    lastAction: VCSRemoteAction? = nil, pullRebase: Bool = true, now: Date
93	  ) -> VCSSyncPresentation {
94	    // [13] A failure outranks everything: it's the only state with something to recover from, and
95	    // burying it under a count would leave the user with no idea the action didn't happen.
96	    if let failure, case .idle = activity {
97	      let message = describe(failure)
98	      let recovery = retryAction(for: failure, lastAction: lastAction)
99	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
100	        // With no recovery to offer, the title must not read as a button. "Retry" over a failure that
101	        // cannot be retried is the whole defect this branch fixes.
102	        titleVariants: recovery == nil ? [] : (lastAction?.label).map { [$0] } ?? ["Retry"],
103	        subtitle: message, subtitleShort: message,
104	        symbol: "exclamationmark.triangle.fill",
105	        action: recovery,
106	        isEnabled: recovery != nil,
107	        // The tooltip is where a failure gets room to explain itself — one line fits the 36pt bar, the
108	        // remedy usually doesn't.
109	        tone: .failure, help: explain(failure, now: now),
110	        accessibility: "\(lastAction?.label ?? "Action") failed. \(explain(failure, now: now))",
111	        lockPath: lockPath(of: failure))
112	    }
113	
114	    // [10/11/12] In flight — one action at a time, so this can't collide with a second.
115	    if case .running(let action) = activity {
116	      let title: String
117	      let subtitle: String
118	      switch action {
119	      case .fetch: (title, subtitle) = ("Fetching…", "from \(state?.primaryRemote ?? "remote")")
120	      case .push: (title, subtitle) = ("Pushing…", "to \(state?.primaryRemote ?? "remote")")
121	      case .pull: (title, subtitle) = ("Pulling…", "from \(state?.primaryRemote ?? "remote")")
122	      case .abortRebase: (title, subtitle) = ("Aborting…", "rebase")
123	      }
124	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
125	        titleVariants: [title], subtitle: subtitle, subtitleShort: subtitle,
126	        symbol: nil, badge: badge(ahead: state?.tracking?.ahead),
127	        action: nil, isEnabled: false, help: "\(title) \(subtitle)",
128	        accessibility: "\(title) \(subtitle)")
129	    }
130	
131	    // [1] Nothing selected.
132	    guard hasTarget else {
133	      return disabled("No workroom selected", symbol: nil)
134	    }
135	    // [2] Selected, but not a readable repo.
136	    guard let state else {
137	      return disabled("No repository", symbol: "exclamationmark.triangle", tone: .warning)
138	    }
139	    // [0] The tools can't run these commands. Nothing below this line could succeed.
140	    guard toolsUsable else {
141	      return disabled(
142	        "Update git to use this", symbol: "exclamationmark.triangle", tone: .warning,
143	        help:
144	          "Fetch, push and pull need a newer git or jj. See the warning for the required version.")
145	    }
146	    // [3] No remote at all.
147	    guard let remote = state.primaryRemote else {
148	      return disabled("No remote configured", symbol: nil)
149	    }
150	
151	    let fetched = fetchedAgo(state.lastFetch, now: now)
152	    let fetchedShort = fetchedAgo(state.lastFetch, now: now, short: true)
153	    let tracking = state.tracking
154	
155	    // [4] No counterpart on the remote yet. This is the DEFAULT state of a fresh workroom —
156	    // `git worktree add -b` sets no upstream — so it must not read as "Push origin" against something
157	    // that doesn't exist.
158	    if let tracking, tracking.gone {
159	      let branch = state.current.name ?? "this branch"
160	      let detail = "\(branch) isn’t on \(remote) yet"
161	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
162	        titleVariants: ["Publish branch", "Publish"],
163	        subtitle: detail, subtitleShort: detail, symbol: "arrow.up.circle",
164	        badge: badge(ahead: tracking.ahead), action: .push, isEnabled: true,
165	        help: "Push \(branch) to \(remote) and start tracking it.",
166	        accessibility: "Publish branch. \(detail)")
167	    }
168	
169	    let ahead = tracking?.ahead ?? 0
170	    let behind = tracking?.behind ?? 0
171	    let pullTitles =
172	      pullRebase
173	      ? ["Pull \(remote) with rebase", "Pull with rebase", "Pull"]
174	      : ["Pull \(remote)", "Pull"]
175	
176	    // [9] Diverged ⇒ Pull, not Push: git refuses a non-fast-forward push, so offering Push here would
177	    // send the user straight into a rejection. Badges show both, ↓ first — the one the action addresses.
178	    if ahead > 0, behind > 0 {
179	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
180	        titleVariants: pullTitles, subtitle: fetched, subtitleShort: fetchedShort,
181	        symbol: "arrow.up.arrow.down",
182	        badge: .init(count: behind, direction: .behind),
183	        secondaryBadge: .init(count: ahead, direction: .ahead),
184	        action: .pull, isEnabled: true,
185	        help:
186	          "\(ahead) to push, \(behind) to pull. Pull first — \(remote) will reject a non-fast-forward push.",
187	        accessibility: "Pull \(remote) with rebase",
188	        accessibilityValue: "\(behind) behind, \(ahead) ahead")
189	    }
190	    // [8] Behind only.
191	    if behind > 0 {
192	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
193	        titleVariants: pullTitles, subtitle: fetched, subtitleShort: fetchedShort,
194	        symbol: "arrow.down", badge: .init(count: behind, direction: .behind),
195	        action: .pull, isEnabled: true,
196	        help: "\(behind) commit\(behind == 1 ? "" : "s") to pull from \(remote). \(fetched).",
197	        accessibility: "Pull \(remote) with rebase", accessibilityValue: "\(behind) behind")
198	    }
199	    // [7] Ahead only.
200	    if ahead > 0 {
201	      return VCSSyncPresentation(
202	        titleVariants: ["Push \(remote)", "Push"], subtitle: fetched, subtitleShort: fetchedShort,
203	        symbol: "arrow.up", badge: .init(count: ahead, direction: .ahead),
204	        action: .push, isEnabled: true,
205	        help: "\(ahead) commit\(ahead == 1 ? "" : "s") to push to \(remote). \(fetched).",
206	        accessibility: "Push \(remote)", accessibilityValue: "\(ahead) ahead")
207	    }
208	    // [5]/[6] In sync — the segment becomes a Fetch button.
209	    return VCSSyncPresentation(
210	      subtitle: fetched, subtitleShort: fetchedShort, symbol: nil,
211	      action: .fetch, isEnabled: true,
212	      help: "Up to date with \(remote). \(fetched). Click to fetch again.",
213	      accessibility: "Fetch \(remote). \(fetched)")
214	  }
215	
216	  private static func disabled(
217	    _ subtitle: String, symbol: String?, tone: VCSSyncPresentation.Tone = .normal,
218	    help: String? = nil
219	  ) -> VCSSyncPresentation {
220	    VCSSyncPresentation(
221	      subtitle: subtitle, subtitleShort: subtitle, symbol: symbol, action: nil, isEnabled: false,
222	      tone: tone, help: help ?? subtitle, accessibility: subtitle)
223	  }
224	
225	  private static func badge(ahead: Int?) -> VCSSyncPresentation.Badge? {
226	    guard let ahead, ahead > 0 else { return nil }
227	    return VCSSyncPresentation.Badge(count: ahead, direction: .ahead)
228	  }
229	
230	  /// Which action a failure offers. `.rebaseInProgress` deliberately offers **Abort**, never a retry —
231	  /// a retry fails identically until the rebase is cleared. `.toolMissing` offers nothing, because no
232	  /// click can fix a missing binary.
233	  static func retryAction(for failure: VCSRemoteFailure, lastAction: VCSRemoteAction?)
234	    -> VCSRemoteAction?
235	  {
236	    switch failure {
237	    case .rebaseInProgress: return .abortRebase
238	    case .rejected: return .pull  // the fix for a rejection is to pull, never to force
239	    case .toolMissing, .noRemote: return nil
240	    // A LOCATED lock file offers nothing, for `rebaseInProgress`'s reason: the file is sitting there, so
241	    // every retry fails identically and the button is a promise that can't be kept. Removing it is the
242	    // only fix and Workroom won't do that for you (see `VCSRemoteFailure.locked`), so the recovery is
243	    // explained rather than offered. An unlocatable lock was transient contention — retry away.
244	    case .locked(let file): return file == nil ? lastAction : nil
245	    default: return lastAction
246	    }
247	  }
248	
249	  /// One-line, actionable copy per failure. The raw stderr is legible for some cases and baffling for
250	  /// others, so the baffling ones get written copy.
251	  static func describe(_ failure: VCSRemoteFailure) -> String {
252	    switch failure {
253	    case .toolMissing(let tool):
254	      return "\(tool) isn’t on Workroom’s PATH."
255	    case .timedOut(let action):
256	      return "\(action.label) timed out."
257	    case .authRequired:
258	      // The #1 expected failure. The runner sets GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0 and ssh BatchMode, so this
259	      // fails instantly rather than hanging — but the raw stderr is baffling, hence bespoke copy.
260	      return "Couldn’t authenticate. Load your key into ssh-agent, or set a credential helper."
261	    case .hostKeyUnverified:
262	      return "The host’s key isn’t known. Connect once from a terminal to accept it."
263	    case .noRemote:
264	      return "No remote configured."
265	    case .rejected:
266	      return "Rejected — the remote has commits you don’t. Pull first."
267	    case .dirtyWorkingTree:
268	      return "Uncommitted changes are in the way. Commit or stash them first."
269	    case .rebaseInProgress:
270	      return "A rebase is in progress. Abort it to continue."
271	    case .locked(let file):
272	      // Two different facts, so two different sentences. Saying "busy, try again" over a lock file that
273	      // is still there sends the user round a loop that cannot terminate.
274	      guard let file else { return "The repository was busy. Try again." }
275	      return "A leftover \(file.filename) is blocking git."
276	    case .other(let message):
277	      return message.split(whereSeparator: \.isNewline).first.map(String.init) ?? "Failed."
278	    }
279	  }
280	
281	  /// The blocking lock file's path, when the failure has one.
282	  static func lockPath(of failure: VCSRemoteFailure) -> String? {
283	    guard case .locked(let file) = failure else { return nil }
284	    return file?.path
285	  }
286	
287	  /// The tooltip form of a failure: `describe`'s one-liner plus, where there is one, the remedy.
288	  ///
289	  /// Only `.locked` currently says more than its subtitle, because it's the only failure whose fix is a
290	  /// thing the user must do OUTSIDE Workroom — and the app deliberately won't do it for them, so the
291	  /// message has to be complete enough to act on: which file, how old, and the caveat that makes the age
292	  /// worth printing. A minutes-old lock with no git running is abandoned; a seconds-old one probably
293	  /// isn't, and that judgement is the user's to make.
294	  static func explain(_ failure: VCSRemoteFailure, now: Date) -> String {
295	    guard case .locked(let file) = failure, let file else { return describe(failure) }
296	    let age = fullFormatter.localizedString(for: file.modifiedAt, relativeTo: now)
297	    return """
298	      A leftover lock file is blocking git.
299	
300	      \(file.path)
301	      Created \(age).
302	
303	      A git command that was force-stopped leaves this behind. If no git command is running for this \
304	      repository, deleting the file is safe:
305	
306	      rm "\(file.path)"
307	      """
308	  }
309	
310	  // MARK: Vocabulary
311	
312	  /// What this backend calls the thing the working copy is on: jj says **bookmark**, git says **branch**.
313	  ///
314	  /// Not cosmetic. A jj bookmark does NOT advance as you commit, which is the defining behaviour of a git
315	  /// branch — so calling it a branch in a jj repo teaches the wrong model of the tool the user is running.
316	  ///
317	  /// A pure function rather than a ternary inside the view because that's the only way it can be tested:
318	  /// the toolbar's caption is not reachable from a unit test, and driving a real jj project through the
319	  /// GUI needs both a selected row and an open terminal.
320	  ///
321	  /// Anything that isn't `"jj"` — including an empty or unrecognised value — reads as "branch". `vcs` comes
322	  /// from the CLI config, so git is the safe default for an unknown, and it matches every non-jj repo the
323	  /// app can currently open.
324	  static func refNoun(vcs: String?) -> String { vcs == "jj" ? "bookmark" : "branch" }
325	
326	  /// The branch segment's caption: "Current Branch" / "Current Bookmark".
327	  static func refCaption(vcs: String?) -> String { "Current \(refNoun(vcs: vcs).capitalized)" }
328	
329	  // MARK: Relative time
330	
331	  private static let fullFormatter: RelativeDateTimeFormatter = {
332	    let f = RelativeDateTimeFormatter()
333	    f.unitsStyle = .full
334	    return f
335	  }()
336	
337	  private static let shortFormatter: RelativeDateTimeFormatter = {
338	    let f = RelativeDateTimeFormatter()
339	    f.unitsStyle = .abbreviated
340	    return f
341	  }()
342	
343	  /// "Fetched 9 minutes ago" / "Fetched 9 min. ago" / "Never fetched" / "".
344	  ///
345	  /// Both forms say "Fetched", never "Last fetched": "ago" already places it in the past, so "Last" only
346	  /// spent width. `short` differs by the formatter's unit style alone.
347	  ///
348	  /// Under a minute reads "just now" rather than "in 0 seconds", which is what
349	  /// `RelativeDateTimeFormatter` produces for a sub-second delta.
350	  ///
351	  /// `.unknown` renders NOTHING — never the word "never". They are different facts: `.never` means we
352	  /// looked and there was no fetch; `.unknown` means we couldn't tell.
353	  static func fetchedAgo(_ lastFetch: VCSLastFetch, now: Date, short: Bool = false) -> String {
354	    switch lastFetch {
355	    case .never: return "Never fetched"
356	    case .unknown: return ""
357	    case .at(let date):
358	      if now.timeIntervalSince(date) < 60 { return "Fetched just now" }
359	      let formatter = short ? shortFormatter : fullFormatter
360	      return "Fetched \(formatter.localizedString(for: date, relativeTo: now))"
361	    }
362	  }
363	}

1	import Foundation

3	/// A VCS action the toolbar can perform.
4	enum VCSRemoteAction: String, Equatable, Sendable, CaseIterable {
5	  case fetch, push, pull, abortRebase
6	
7	  var label: String {
8	    switch self {
9	    case .fetch: return "Fetch"
10	    case .push: return "Push"
11	    case .pull: return "Pull"
12	    case .abortRebase: return "Abort rebase"
13	    }
14	  }
15	
16	  /// Whether the action contacts a remote — drives the timeout budget and whether the command needs
17	  /// the auth-forwarding environment (`StatusCommandRunner.runNetwork`).
18	  var touchesNetwork: Bool { self != .abortRebase }
19	}
20	
21	/// Why a remote read or action failed.
22	///
23	/// Deliberately NOT folded into `VCSError`: that enum is the backend-*read* taxonomy
24	/// (`lockContention`/`staleSnapshot`/`partialData`/…) and `WorkroomStatusResolver.failure(for:)`
25	/// switches over it exhaustively to choose a sidebar badge. `.authRequired` has no sidebar badge and
26	/// no sensible answer there, so adding it would force a meaningless decision in a function that
27	/// currently has a principled one for every case. Same reasoning that put `CIResolution`/`PRResolution`
28	/// beside their resolver instead of in `VCSModels.swift`.
29	enum VCSRemoteFailure: Equatable, Sendable {
30	  /// `git`/`jj` not on PATH. Distinct from `VCSToolVersions`' floor check, which runs at launch —
31	  /// this is the same condition caught at the point of use.
32	  case toolMissing(String)
33	  case timedOut(VCSRemoteAction)
34	  /// Credentials were needed and none were available.
35	  case authRequired(String)
36	  /// The host's key isn't in `known_hosts`. `BatchMode=yes` turns what would be an interactive
37	  /// confirmation into this, so it needs its own copy — telling the user to configure a credential
38	  /// helper would be wrong advice.
39	  case hostKeyUnverified(String)
40	  case noRemote
41	  /// Push rejected (non-fast-forward). The engine NEVER force-pushes; the UI offers Pull.
42	  case rejected(String)
43	  /// git refused because tracked files would be overwritten.
44	  case dirtyWorkingTree(String)
45	  /// A failed or killed `git pull --rebase` left `rebase-merge`/`rebase-apply` behind. The repo needs
46	  /// `git rebase --abort`, so the UI must offer that instead of a retry that will fail identically.
47	  case rebaseInProgress
48	  /// A repo lock was held — git `index.lock`/`packed-refs.lock`, or jj's `git_import_export.lock`.
49	  ///
50	  /// The payload is the lock file itself when we could find it on disk, and that distinction decides
51	  /// what the UI offers. **`nil` ⇒ transient contention**, so Retry is genuine: another command held the
52	  /// lock briefly and by the next click it is likely gone. **Non-nil ⇒ a lock file is sitting there
53	  /// right now**, and retrying fails identically every time — the same reasoning that makes
54	  /// `rebaseInProgress` offer Abort instead of Retry.
55	  ///
56	  /// A leftover lock is what a SIGKILLed git leaves: the runner escalates to `killTree` two seconds
57	  /// after SIGTERM, and SIGKILL cannot be caught, so git's own cleanup never runs.
58	  ///
59	  /// Workroom does NOT delete it. Whether a lock is truly abandoned or held by a git running right now
60	  /// is not knowable from outside the process — `lsof` can't be trusted for it, and removing a live
61	  /// lock corrupts the index — so this reports and explains, and the removal stays the user's call.
62	  /// That is also what git's own message tells you to do.
63	  case locked(VCSLockFile?)
64	  case other(String)
65	}
66	
67	/// A lock file found blocking a VCS operation.
68	///
69	/// Located by parsing the path out of git's own error, which names it exactly, then stat-ing it — so the
70	/// file reported is the one git actually complained about rather than a guess at which lock it might be.
71	struct VCSLockFile: Equatable, Sendable {
72	  let path: String
73	  let modifiedAt: Date
74	
75	  var filename: String { (path as NSString).lastPathComponent }
76	}
77	
78	/// What a remote-state read decided. Mirrors `CIResolution`/`PRResolution`, `keepPrior` included: a
79	/// transient blip must not blank a good toolbar.
80	enum VCSRemoteResolution: Equatable, Sendable {
81	  case state(VCSRemoteState)
82	  /// Not a git/jj repo, or a repo with no refs at all (a fresh `git init`).
83	  case absent
84	  case keepPrior
85	  case failed(VCSRemoteFailure)
86	}
87	
88	/// What an action decided.
89	///
90	/// There is deliberately no `okWithConflicts`: jj records conflicts *inside* commits and `jj rebase`
91	/// exits 0 when it produces them, so the exit code cannot distinguish them — and the working-copy read
92	/// that could is not safe to make here (it would re-enter `JJSnapshotGate` for the same project root,
93	/// which that type documents as a deadlock). `RemoteStateModel` upgrades a `.ok` pull to "conflicted"
94	/// from the status refresh it already triggers, after the gate has released.
95	enum VCSRemoteActionResult: Equatable, Sendable {
96	  case ok(summary: String)
97	  case failed(VCSRemoteFailure)
98	}
99	
100	/// The seam for VCS operations that **write** — remote state reads plus fetch/push/pull.
